newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks snap three-day skid to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks snap three-day skid to end higher.

text.p: Swiss shares firmed more than one percent on Tuesday to end slightly below the day's highs, regaining the 4,500-point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after a three-day fall.

The firming U.S. dollar and friendly U.S. and domestic bond markets were seen as the main reasons for the advance. "Today has been a dollar day," one trader said, citing sizeable gains in dollar-sensitive industrials.
The SMI added 53.6 points, or 1.2 percent, to 4,513.7. The all-share Swiss Performance Index ended up 29.77 points, or 1.05 percent, at 2,867.76.

Shares of engineering group ABB, which have suffered in the past few sessions after posting lower-than-expected 1996 results, were among the day's biggest winners. ABB added 48 francs, or almost three percent, to 1,729.
Most-active Novartis registered shares were up 29 francs to 1,701. Roche certificates were up 70 francs to 12,260.

Subscription rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals shares (CSC) were up 5.40 francs to 97.40 amid sold retail demand. CSC shares may now be priced above the indicated range of 72 to 86 francs per share for a global offering, co-lead organisers UBS and CSFB said.

Financials, which had outperformed industrials on Monday, lagged the rest of the market. UBS bearer shares gave up 0.50 francs to 265.50. Credit Suisse, which is due to release its 1996 results on Wednesday, added 0.75 francs to 158.50.
Zurich Insurance added seven francs to 1,508.
Bearer shares of watchmaker SMH were up six francs at 860.
